parts.latex:
His brother, Jake, finds an account that will earn him $12\%$ per annum. The interest will also be compounded quarterly.

However, Jake is only prepared to contribute for 2 years.

Find the amount that he must contribute quarterly if he is to achieve the same future value as Tom.
parts.note: Annuity future-value interest-factor table look-up (2024 Advanced uses the GP formula only; moved to Standard).

solutions.latex:
Interest is compounded quarterly, so the rate per period is $\dfrac{8}{4} = 2\%$ and the number of periods is $3\times 4 = 12$.

From the table, the factor for $2\%$ and $12$ periods is $13.4121$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Future value} &= 750 \times 13.4121 \\ &= \$10059.08 \end{aligned}$$

For Jake, the rate per period is $\dfrac{12}{4} = 3\%$ and the number of periods is $2\times 4 = 8$.

From the table, the factor is $8.8923$. Let his quarterly contribution be $\$M$.
$$\begin{aligned} M \times 8.8923 &= 10059.08 \\ M &= \$1131.21 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A flagpole, $BD$, lies on flat level ground.

It is supported by two cables, $AD$ and $CD$ as shown below. The cable $AD$ is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal and is tied 18 metres from the foot of the pole.

The second cable is tied at a point, $C$, 12m from $A$ and on a bearing of $210^\circ$ from $A$.

\exfigure{1310_q13c_1}

Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.
parts.note: 3D trigonometry (flagpole with ground cables and a bearing): now Year 11 Extension 1, not Advanced.

solutions.latex:
In the right-angled triangle $BAD$, $\tan 30^\circ=\dfrac{BD}{18}$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} &= \dfrac{BD}{18} \\ BD &= \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{3}} = 6\sqrt{3} \end{aligned}$$
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=18$, $AC=12$ and $\angle BAC=60^\circ$. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} BC^2 &= 18^2+12^2-2(18)(12)\cos 60^\circ \\ &= 468-216 \\ &= 252 \end{aligned}$$
$$BC=\sqrt{252}=6\sqrt{7}$$
In the right-angled triangle $BCD$:
$$\begin{aligned} \tan\theta &= \dfrac{BD}{BC} \\ &= \dfrac{6\sqrt{3}}{6\sqrt{7}} \\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta\approx 33^\circ$$
criteria: Correct value of $BC$ (allowing for errors carried forward), or equivalent merit
Expression for $BC^2$, even if $\angle BAC$ is incorrect, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source does not show why $\angle BAC=60^\circ$ (from the bearing of $210^\circ$ and the diagram); stated it as the angle used. A solution diagram (bearings and triangles) would help but was not added here.

solutions.latex:
Compounded half-yearly, so the rate per period and number of periods are
$$\begin{aligned} r &= \dfrac{2\%}{2} = 1\% \text{ per half-year} \\ n &= 4\times 2 = 8 \end{aligned}$$
From the table, the interest factor is $8.2857$.

Using future value $=$ present value $\times$ interest factor:
$$\begin{aligned} 34800 &= \text{present value}\times 8.2857 \\ \text{present value} &= \dfrac{34800}{8.2857} \\ &\approx \$4200 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is B.

In a chess tournament, each player has a 'chess rating', which is a value from 1600 to 2000.

Danny wants to know if there is a correlation between the number of years a player has spent playing chess and their chess rating.

Danny randomly surveyed 10 players at the tournament. The results are shown in the table.

\extable{1312_q12_t1}

Beth, a competitor in the tournament, has spent 5 years playing chess.

Use the equation of the least-squares regression line for this data set to determine Beth's chess rating. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
parts.note: Least-squares regression line (bivariate data) is Mathematics Standard, not 2024 Advanced.

solutions.latex:
The least-squares regression line has the form $y = Bx + A$.

From the calculator, $A \approx 1554.49$ and $B \approx 34.64$, so
$$y = 34.64x + 1554.49$$
When $x=5$:
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 34.64\times5+1554.49 \\ &\approx 1727.69 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore, Beth's chess rating is predicted to be $1728$.
criteria: Correctly provides the equation of the least-squares regression line, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source quoted full calculator values A = 1554.492754, B = 34.63768116; shown here rounded to 2 dp as in the source line.
